about: Real advertising claims ruled on by the UK ASA (public rulings). Records are PARAPHRASED from the ASA pages by an AI reader; the source URL is the authority. Labels (upheld / not upheld) are the regulator's, not ours. Harvested 2026-11-15 (rate-limited pages retried successfully with a plain browser user agent). Some fields may contain reader errors: verify against the ruling before publishing any figure.
known_data_discrepancies: Luxury Lodges: headline says up to 83,454 over two years; the ruling's assessment text says 83,354
ULEZProsperity website: ruling says 37-month rental period; advertiser's response says 38 months

in_scope_real_estate.kind: off-plan London tower marketed to buy-to-let investors (rental factsheet)

claims.text: Estimated weekly rents and estimated average gross yields per unit type were representative and achievable (1-bed 3.9-4.9%, 2-bed 4.5-4.6%, 3-bed 2.9-3.8%, 3-bed duplex 3.1-3.5%; weekly rents 1-bed 745-925, 2-bed 1115-1335, 3-bed 1750-2500)
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: estimates not substantiated against comparable achieved rents; most rent ranges above achieved rents at a nearby tower

claims.text: Gross yields shown with no explanation of how they were calculated
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: basis of projection not apparent

in_scope_real_estate.evidence_asa_examined: Achieved rents at a nearby tower (per LonRes): 1-bed 700-750/week, 2-bed 1100-2150/week, 3-bed 2095-2308/week; no data found for 3-bed duplexes. The advertiser's evidence relied on asking prices from a single tower and included penthouses, duplexes and properties outside the postcode.

in_scope_real_estate.kind: holiday lodge property investment with a rental-income guarantee (magazine ad)

claims.text: Guaranteed return of up to about 83,454 over two years, based on historical success, from 295,000
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: ambiguous whether return refers to rent or value; guarantee not explained

claims.text: No warning that investment values can fall; 'historical success' with no past-performance qualifier
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: missing risk

claims.text: From 295,000 price shown without ongoing non-optional charges
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: material cost omitted

in_scope_real_estate.context_in_ruling: 80% minimum occupancy; shortfall made up after 12 months; guarantee runs 12 to 24 months

in_scope_real_estate.kind: land auction investment (social and web ads)

claims.text: Land investments return 10-30% ROI
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: two case studies, one old, did not show the return was generally achievable

claims.text: No warning that investment value can go down
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: missing risk

claims.text: Selling land at auction achieves much higher prices than using an estate agent
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: compared valuations with sold prices; no evidence difference was caused by the auction method

in_scope_real_estate.evidence_asa_examined: Case 1: plot valued at 25,000, sold for 48,500, split into lots totalling 138,500. Case 2: plot valued at 950,000, split into 20 lots totalling 1,242,000 (30% increase).

in_scope_real_estate.kind: training for investing in land (social and web ads); property-adjacent, not a listing

claims.text: Six-figure profits and financial freedom with no warning values can fall
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: missing risk

claims.text: Helped hundreds of clients; client results shown without 'past performance is not a guide'
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: unrepresentative examples, no qualifier

claims.text: One client made 350K on a deal; clients made 6,000,000 profit this year; profits of 100K to half a million possible
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: no evidence supplied for objective profit claims

in_scope_real_estate.kind: retirement apartment sales marketing; savings claims

claims.text: Downsizing to a Churchill apartment saves over 1,000 a year on energy (video cites 1,160)
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: comparison apartment was an unusually efficient B-rated heat-pump development; not representative

claims.text: Downsizing saves about 2,300 a year overall
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: comparison homes used far more energy than typical homes; basis not qualified

claims.text: Cost-of-living narrative on the web page
claims.label: flawed
claims.outcome: upheld for the web page only
claims.flaw: likely to cause fear or distress without justification (not a numbers flaw)

claims.text: Same narrative in the paid Facebook post
claims.label: sound

in_scope_real_estate.evidence_asa_examined: Churchill estimated saving range 2,260-2,740. Comparison homes used 24,255 and 27,560 kWh a year; Ofgem typical medium household 14,200 kWh, high 21,100 kWh. Apartments used were 25% below their development's average.

in_scope_real_estate.kind: estate agency comparison against three named competitors (leaflet and Facebook post)

claims.text: Your personal agent all the way
claims.label: sound

claims.text: Accompanied viewings by your personal agent
claims.label: sound

claims.text: Number 1 in the world for home sales volume (read as the brand)
claims.label: sound

claims.text: Personal social media campaign (shown as unique to the advertiser)
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: competitors also offer it

claims.text: Personalised sale board for maximum marketing effect
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: competitors also offer it

claims.text: Same day feedback on all viewings
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: presented as guaranteed and superior; not substantiated

claims.text: Skilled negotiations by an agent who knows your home
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: subjective, no objective standard

claims.text: Nine-criteria comparison table ticking the advertiser on all nine and competitors on two
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: footnote cited 'research of each agency's standard package' with no sources or date

claims.text: Rent first and buy within 12 months to get nine months' rent back or 5% off the asking price
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: key conditions in tiny print; asterisk attached to only one of the two offers. NOT a reasoning flaw: an omission/layout flaw

in_scope_real_estate.kind: new-build flats; image vs headline price (website)

claims.text: Show-home bathroom photo shown next to a 'from' price
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: bathroom had upgrades not included in the price. Image/price mismatch, not a reasoning flaw. Old (2012)

in_scope_real_estate.kind: off-plan London E14 flats pitched to investors by email

claims.text: Prices in the area are expected to rise at least 5-10% over the next 18 months and already have, which equates to a 50-100% return on the actual investment
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: advertiser's only valid support was a 43% borough-wide average price rise in one past year; that does not show these particular properties will rise 5-10%. Arithmetic in the advertiser's reply is internally consistent: the flaw is the conclusion, not the sums

claims.text: No statement that past performance is not a guide or that values can fall as well as rise
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: missing risk and past-performance qualifier

claims.text: The 50-100% return figure gives no basis for how it was calculated
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: basis of projection not apparent

in_scope_real_estate.evidence_in_ruling: Advertiser's worked example (from its reply): unit price 430,000; 10% deposit (43,000); 5% a year growth over 18 months gives value 462,787, a gain of 32,787 = 76% return on the deposit; 10% growth gives 155%. Evidence offered: a 2014 newspaper article on Tower Hamlets average prices up 43% (May 2013 to May 2014).
in_scope_real_estate.note: Best 'right numbers, wrong conclusion' case in the set

in_scope_real_estate.kind: estate agent leaflet in Chalfont St Peter

claims.text: Up to 10% higher sale prices than other local estate agents
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: compares final sale prices with other agents' initial valuations (not a fair comparison); support was vendor testimonials; based on only 13 sales

claims.text: We are the only local estate agent open seven days a week
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: 'local' undefined; agents in the neighbouring town were open seven days

claims.text: Leaflet sent to a rival's customers without warning about possible double fees under a sole-agency contract
claims.label: sound

in_scope_real_estate.evidence_in_ruling: Advertiser said 13 sales completed, two more than 10% above another agent's valuation; examples cited 10.8%, 10.6% and 5.9% above initial valuation.

in_scope_real_estate.kind: online estate agent TV ad and website savings claims

claims.text: You could save thousands (small print cites a 2011 Which? survey of average agent commission)
claims.label: sound
claims.why_sound: ASA found evidence weak but read the claim loosely: fixed fees mean an agent would need very low commission for no saving to arise

claims.text: 4,158 average customer saving when selling
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: evidence was UK average asking prices (not Purplebricks' own sold prices) and a single conveyancing firm's email for the 1.5% average commission; no sales data to show how the average was derived

claims.text: Saving claim could be checked by consumers or competitors
claims.label: flawed
claims.flaw: ad did not disclose the average sale price used or link to the calculation

in_scope_real_estate.evidence_in_ruling: Average UK asking price 303,190; assumed average agent commission 1.5%; Purplebricks fixed fees 798 outside London, 1,158 in Greater London (inc. VAT). A simple recompute from these disclosed inputs does not give 4,158 (1.5% of 303,190 is 4,547.85; minus the fees gives about 3,390 to 3,750).
